items.title: fix(desktop): preserve Zip64 counts in exported ZIP views
items.body:
## Summary

An exported desktop environment reports a healthy ZIP as `not a readable zip archive` when its selected `zip_entries` exceeds 65,535. The bounded directory already has a Zip64 end record, but the Python reader also packs the full retained count into the classic end record's 16-bit fields. At 65,536 files, `struct.pack` overflows and the reader misclassifies its own framing failure as archive damage.

Reproduced with a ZIP independently written and read by Python's standard-library `zipfile`, on main `3676ec632bfbe4fde2f5303daa0d9261072ce04a`. No related count-serialization PR was found. Existing #9173/#10618 address input Zip64 record location; this repair concerns the exported reader's generated decoder copy.

## Change

Give bounded-directory framing one `_zip_directory_tail` owner. Preserve exact Zip64 counts, size, offset and locator coordinates; saturate the classic 16-bit count and 32-bit size/offset fields at their format-defined sentinels. The requested listing is preserved rather than capped at 65,535.

Keep directory selection, prepended-data offset handling, per-member/total-byte/ratio limits, integrity checks and archive ordering intact. Document raised listing policies. This changes existing offline desktop views without adding target execution or provider authority.

## Executed validation

Linux, Node 24.22.1 / npm 11.9.0:

- The unchanged reader fails the real 65,536-file producer witness with `not a readable zip archive`; the repaired reader preserves the complete listing.
- **69 targeted tests across four files passed**: seven count/offset cases, 25 existing ZIP parity/resource/integrity regressions, 36 exporter/renderer cases, and one public CLI export case.
- A genuine 65,537-file archive qualifies selections of 1,000 / 65,535 / 65,536 / 65,537, exact first/last names, source counts, policy truncation and unchanged source bytes. Native bounded-directory selection agrees.
- The public `export-desktop-application --view-policy ...` case executes the exact emitted Python reader and verifies its 65,536-file policy/listing. Its capture uses a small seed; the large archive represents later application state. The AgentEnv framework is not required or exercised.
- Wide-offset wire cases inspect classic, Zip64 and locator fields around `0xffffffff`, without allocating or claiming to read a 4 GiB archive.
- Required build, `npm run check:fast`, normal commit/pre-push hooks and `git diff --check` passed. Scoped typed lint: four files, **zero errors and zero warnings**. All **3734** test/spec files are discovered exactly once.
- `npm run docs:check`: six tasks and eight README consistency tests passed.

Large-count cases deliberately retain the existing one-byte member budget, so two-byte payloads remain explicitly unread while listing all selected identities. They qualify directory fidelity, not decompression of every large-archive member. Existing ZIP regressions separately exercise readable contents, CRC/size failures, Unicode names and resource ceilings. No timeout or heap allowance was raised. Native Windows/macOS, the complete monolithic suite and a live AgentEnv computer were not run. Hosted CI remains pending for the published head.

```sh
npm run test:focused -- src/domain/desktop/appExport.test.ts
npm run test:focused -- tests/boundary/cli/desktopZip64CountCli.test.ts
```

## Summary

A valid Zip64 archive with an extensible end record can lose its entire desktop state view, or appear empty when extension bytes resemble another end record. Follow the locator's declared frame before the existing fixed-record fallback in both REA and the generated Python reader. This also lets an exported task grade the retained archive correctly.

Found independently through the production readers and a compiled CLI control. No issue was opened only to link the fix.

## Problem and expected behavior

On frozen main `98c589e42019b4cc2c3c6aee1f6d2031e2de2441`, a 218-byte authored archive containing `settings.json` is readable by the unwrapped ZIP library, but both desktop readers return `not a readable zip archive`. A fixed-size Zip64 control passes.

The Zip64 end record has a 56-byte fixed header followed by optional opaque extension bytes. Both readers instead assumed the record began exactly 56 bytes before its locator. A record-looking tail inside an extension was consequently treated as the end record and silently reduced a nonempty archive to zero entries. Four regressions fail on the frozen production files: deferred/classic end fields, each with a short extension or a misleading tail.

[PKWARE APPNOTE 4.3.14-4.3.15](https://pkware.cachefly.net/webdocs/casestudies/APPNOTE.TXT) defines the variable extensible sector, the size excluding the leading 12 bytes, and the locator's record offset. Unknown extension contents must not replace the located directory frame.

items.title: fix(desktop): read a Zip64 end record that carries an extensible data sector
items.body:
## Summary

`directoryEnd` located the Zip64 end-of-central-directory record by subtracting its fixed 56 bytes from the locator. [APPNOTE 4.3.14](https://libzip.org/specifications/appnote_iz.txt) lets that record end with a variable-size extensible data sector, so a conforming archive whose record carries one was refused as `not a readable zip archive` with no entries listed.

## Measured

A one-member Zip64 archive whose record ends with N extensible bytes, on this host:

| extensible bytes | before | after | `unzip -l` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 1 entry | 1 entry | lists `a.txt` |
| 8 | **refused** | 1 entry | lists `a.txt` |
| 32 | **refused** | 1 entry | lists `a.txt` |
| 1024 | **refused** | 1 entry | lists `a.txt` |

Info-ZIP `unzip` lists the member of every one of those archives, so the refusal is an accept/reject flip against a reference reader, not a stricter reading of the format.

## Approach

4.3.15 has the locator declare the record's offset, so the declared offset is read first. A record can only end where its locator begins, and only the record's own length field says where it begins — so that length must land exactly on the locator. That check is what distinguishes the real record from a coincidental signature, and it keeps the refusal when a declared offset points at something else.

When the declared offset does not land there, the fixed 56 bytes before the locator are read first, as `zipfile` and `zip.js` do, and then the bytes behind them are walked for the record's real start, bounded by `ZIP64_EXTENSIBLE_LIMIT`.

A declared archive offset cannot account for data prepended to the archive, so the walk also makes that case work:

| prepended bytes | extensible | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 0 | 1 entry | 1 entry |
| 0 | 8 | **refused** | 1 entry |
| 16 | 0 | 1 entry | 1 entry |
| 16 | 8 | **refused** | 1 entry |

## Evidence

- `src/domain/desktop/zipDirectory.test.ts` — new file, 2 cases covering both tables above. Reverting the source fails both (`2 failed`), and no test previously called `scanZipDirectory` at all.
- The existing Zip64 tests (`tests/boundary/providers/desktopZipPython.test.ts:388,405`) build their archives with `withZip64End`, which always writes a 44-byte body hard against its locator — the shape that cannot see this defect.
- `src/domain/desktop`, `src/domain/apkSignature`, `src/domain/zipEndOfCentralDirectory.test.ts` — 1012 passing. The single `appWithheld` failure reproduces on `main` on this Windows host.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` — 0 errors. `npm run lint` — 0 errors.

Unavailable coverage: `desktopZipPython` and `desktopZipHeap` exercise this path only through Python and a subprocess, and the former fails 26 tests on this Windows host at both revisions. The new test calls `scanZipDirectory` directly, so it runs everywhere.

items.title: fix(zip): account 64-bit data descriptors that MSIX packages write
items.body:
## Summary

ZIP listings of MSIX and APPX packages reported `unknown` coverage with a "ZIP central directory does not account for N byte(s)" limitation, though the packages are well formed. The unaccounted bytes were each member's own data descriptor. They are now accounted for, and these listings report `complete` coverage.

Fixes #11729

## Problem and expected behavior

MSIX and APPX writers defer every compressed member's CRC and sizes to a signed data descriptor with 8-byte sizes (24 bytes in all). Neither the local header nor the central directory record has a ZIP64 extra field. From `OneDriveSync.msix`, read with Python's `zipfile`:

```
AppxManifest.xml flag=0x8 local crc/csize/usize=0x0/0x0/0x0
   local extra: []
   central: crc 0xfff55929 csize 4135 usize 18338 (no extra field)
   after data: 504b0708 2959f5ff 2710000000000000 a247000000000000
```

`dataDescriptorBytes` chose the descriptor width from `record.zip64`. That flag is false here, so only the 12-byte body was tried. It did not match, and all 24 bytes counted as unaccounted.

## Change and scope

- `dataDescriptorBytes` in `src/domain/zip/zipMemberRegion.ts` tries both size widths, the record's own width first. Each layout still has to match the recorded CRC (when known) and both sizes.
- The same change accepts the converse layout: a ZIP64 directory record followed by a 32-bit descriptor.
- No other accounting rule changes. Prepended bytes, unlisted local entries and malformed signing blocks are still reported.

Contribution scope: ordinary fix within existing boundaries; maintainer scope decision not applicable.

## Contract and boundary impact

- Semantic owner and earliest changed stage: `accountZipMemberRegion` / `dataDescriptorBytes` in `src/domain/zip/zipMemberRegion.ts`; `ZipArtifactReader` consumes its account.
- Contribution scope fit and linked maintainer decision: not applicable.
- CLI and MCP/tool-catalog contract: none.
- Provider, bridge, target-format, or platform compatibility: MSIX/APPX listings now report `complete`; other ZIPs are unchanged.
- Evidence, artifact, provenance, or reconstruction contract: coverage for these packages goes from `unknown` to `complete`; the limitation text is unchanged.
- Target selection, authority, upstream behavior, and cleanup details: not applicable.
- Generated metadata, package, or installation impact: none.

- [x] Read existing files or captured data.

## Evidence and regression coverage

- Tests added or updated: two cases in `src/artifacts/ZipMemberRegion.test.ts`. One builds an MSIX-shaped archive (flag 0x8, zeroed local CRC and sizes, 24-byte signed descriptors, no ZIP64 fields) and lists it through `ZipArtifactReader`. The other accounts a 32-bit descriptor after a record marked ZIP64.
- Base reproduction: the file on main 4ea24b6f8: 2 failed / 15 passed (both new cases). With this change: 17 passed.
- Real packages: I ran `rea inspect-artifact --format json` over 732 ZIP files on one Windows machine. On main, 85 of 85 MSIX and 2 of 3 APPX packages had the limitation. Every range was 24 bytes. With this change, 0 of those 88 have it. The 644 other ZIPs (Ghidra and JDK jars, whl, npz, PyTorch `.pt`, docx/pptx/xlsx, plain zip) had no limitation before or after.
- User-visible CLI/MCP output, before, for an Edge WebView2 `identity_helper.Sparse.Stable.msix`:


items.body:
> **Stacked on #8988**, which builds on the desktop stack merged as #8954. This branch contains #8988. Review only `5981aa78b` and the merges `d97208018`, `7185bd02c`, `87bb4a8aa`, `e76a16334`, `deb1d754d` and `330f9e226`, which bring in #8988's review fixes. The merge keeps the namespace refusal removed, so a check on a whole `.odt` listing is accepted. It also moves the exported XML reader into `appExportPythonXml.ts` to keep `appExportPython.ts` under the 500-line limit. Once #8988 merges, the diff shrinks to these. It is about 330 added and 280 removed lines, most of them the Python reader and its parity tests.

## Summary

Desktop task checks can now point into namespaced XML, such as Inkscape SVGs and the `content.xml` inside LibreOffice and other ODF documents. Before this change, the export refused such checks because REA's view and the exported Python reader spelled namespaced names differently.

## Problem and expected behavior

A five-app scorecard on #8988 hit this on two apps. Inkscape saves `poster.svg` with the SVG namespace both as the default and as `svg:`, plus `inkscape:` and `sodipodi:` attributes. Writer saves `content.xml` with `office:`, `text:` and `style:` names. REA's TypeScript view kept names as the document spells them (`text:p`, `sodipodi:docname`). The exported reader used ElementTree, which spells them `{urn:oasis:names:tc:opendocument:xmlns:text:1.0}p`. A check written against REA's view therefore could not pass in the verifier, so export refused it. The only checks left for these apps were that a file exists.

After this change, the export accepts these checks, and both evaluators fail them before the edit and pass them after:

```json
[
  {"id": "headline", "kind": "value_equals", "file": "Pictures/poster.svg",
   "pointer": "/root/children/[name=g][@inkscape:label=Layer 1]/children/[name=text][@id=headline]/children/[name=tspan]/children/0",
   "value": "Summer Bake Sale"},
  {"id": "date", "kind": "value_equals", "file": "Documents/flyer.odt",
   "pointer": "/entries/[name=content.xml]/view/root/children/[name=office:body]/children/[name=office:text]/children/[name=text:p][@text:style-name=Subtitle]/children/0",
   "value": "Monday 24 November"}
]
```

## Change and scope

- **One naming rule.** Both readers name elements and attributes exactly as the document writes them, prefix included. An element in a default namespace gets its bare name. Namespace declarations stay as ordinary `xmlns` and `xmlns:PREFIX` attributes, in document order.
    - **REA's view is unchanged:** this is what it already produced, so existing views and pointers keep working. Only the Python side moved.
    - **Why not `{uri}local` in both:** it would change every existing view and pointer, and it cannot be mapped back to a prefix when a document binds one namespace twice, as Inkscape does.
- **Python reader.** `xml.parsers.expat` replaces ElementTree, in two passes:
    1. **With namespace processing.** It only checks the document, so it refuses what it refused before: an undeclared prefix, one attribute under two prefixes, `xmlns:p=""`, `a:b:c`, and a processing-instruction target with a colon. DOCTYPEs are still refused.
    2. **Without namespace processing.** A streaming reader builds the view within the same 5,000-node and depth-64 limits, with the same whitespace and `xml:space` rules. It builds only the nodes it keeps, where the old code built a tree of the whole file.
    - **Text** splits where REA's DOM splits it: at CDATA sections, comments and processing instructions. An empty CDATA section joins the text around it.
- **Export and draft.** The namespace refusal is removed, along with `namesXmlNamespace`. The task draft no longer skips namespaced XML, in plain files or in zip entries. For the `.odt` it suggests `[name=text:p][@text:style-name=Subtitle]`.
- **Docs.** The state, tasks and export guides, with the example checks above. Also the `document-views` and `tasks` specs, with the "XML names / CDATA" known difference removed.

## Contract and boundary impact

- **Semantic owner and earliest changed stage:** the exported Python reader in `appExportPython.ts`; REA's own view is unchanged.
- **Contribution scope fit and linked maintainer decision:** same approved desktop-environments work as #8874; this closes the namespaced-XML follow-up listed on #8988.

All 11 new or changed behavior tests fail on the parent commit and pass here. The refactored zip and FreeCAD tests pass on both.

    - the SVG and `.odt` views are equal between the readers;

items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #2377.

Adds `inspect_jvm_debug_metadata` / `inspect-jvm-debug-metadata`, a static, in-process reader of the compiler-emitted debug metadata in a local `.class` file or in a class entry of a `.jar`. Multi-release JARs are supported through an explicit `release`. It lets an analyst or agent judge **debugging readiness before attaching a debugger**: which methods carry line numbers and local-variable names, which were stripped, and which are malformed.

## Problem and expected behavior

Before this change, an analyst had to run `javap -l` or open a decompiler, then read per-method tables by hand, to answer "can I debug this class with names and lines?". Decompiler line numbers are not compiler positions, so they cannot answer it.

Expected: one bounded call returns the following, as artifact-bound Evidence, without executing Java:

- per-method readiness (`present | partial | stripped | malformed | not-applicable`);
- source file;
- line positions and local declarations;
- out-of-range scopes.

## Change and scope

- `src/domain/jvm/`: a dependency-free JVMS §4.7 reader using `Result` and tagged errors, bounded before allocation.
  - It decodes `SourceFile`, `SourceDebugExtension` (kept opaque), `LineNumberTable`, `LocalVariableTable` and `LocalVariableTypeTable`.
  - It binds offsets, slots and scopes to each method's name and descriptor.
  - It checks `max_locals`, code length and constant-pool kinds.
  - Repeated or trailing attributes are reported as malformed, never silently merged.
- `src/jvm/`: the provider and lifecycle.
  - **JAR descriptor and cleanup:** one owned JAR descriptor through `withArtifactRegularFile`, with cleanup leases and retained failed-close ownership, following the RustBinaryProvider pattern.
  - **Classification:** the archive is classified by a magic peek before the class-file budget is applied.
  - **Multi-release selection:** decided exactly as JDK 25's `JarFile` does (`src/jvm/jarManifest.ts` ports `Attributes.read`).
    - The manifest is matched by a case-insensitive stored name and follows the JDK's last-duplicate rule.
    - Manifests over 16,000,000 bytes count as not multi-release, mirroring the default `jdk.jar.maxSignatureFileSize`.
    - Version directories are limited to 9..2147483647.
    - Versions are never silently combined.
  - **JAR reading:** REA opens a JAR with its own reader (`src/artifacts/JdkZipCentralDirectory.ts`, `src/artifacts/JdkZipFile.ts`). It reproduces OpenJDK 25's `ZipFile`: `findEND`, `initCEN`, `checkAndAddEntry`, `checkExtraFields`, `countCENHeaders` and `getInputStream`, over raw bytes.
    - It refuses the whole archive exactly where `new JarFile(...)` does, quoting the JDK's message: encrypted records, bad compression methods, END and zip64 inconsistencies, and so on.
    - It reads members from the central directory alone, as the JDK does. It makes no CRC or local-header cross-check, and charges the decompression budget with the bytes actually produced.
    - The manifest is read as `JarFile.getBytes` reads it.
    - A shared zip.js-based reader could not be made exact, because zip.js reads END, zip64 END and local headers differently. The JVM tool therefore no longer uses `ZipArtifactReader`.
    - `inspect_artifact` still lists JARs through the shared reader, so on an unusual JAR the two tools can disagree. Each tool's docs state its own rule.
  - **Member matching:** JAR members are matched by their stored names, independent of ZIP attribute bits. `./`-prefixed members are inert, as for the JDK, and `META-INF/` entries are never versioned. Symlink-mode members are read as ZIP bytes, as JDK 25 reads them; no host link is followed.
- Shared ZIP reader (`src/artifacts/`; #4473 carries the same changes, and the JVM tool no longer uses this reader):
  - **`storedPath`:** `ArtifactEntry.storedPath` is the raw central-directory name, never the Info-ZIP Unicode Path name. A limitation is recorded when the two differ.
  - **Directory rule:** a member is a directory only when its stored name ends in `/`.
  - **Attribute-only directories:** members marked as directories only by attribute bits are readable files with a limitation. This makes two shapes fail closed with explicit errors:
    - `foo` plus `foo/bar` is a prefix conflict;
    - `.` or an empty name is a non-normalized path.
  - **Reused helper:** `peekArtifactMagic` reuses `readStableArtifact`'s no-follow, identity-checked open.
- Wiring: contract, CLI, MCP, composition, effects, catalog provider identity, docs, skill routing, and `npm run verify:jvm` with its fixtures.

Not included: decompilation, source resolution, and any runtime or debugger attachment.

Scope: [contribution scope](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contribution-scope). This is static format inspection of a caller-selected local file within existing offline-artifact authority. No Java executes, nothing is fetched, and nothing is mutated. No maintainer scope decision is required.

- Semantic owner and earliest changed stage:
  - `src/domain/jvm/javaDebugMetadata.ts` (meaning of the attributes);

items.title: feat(desktop): read zipped documents and name XML elements in task checks
items.body:
> Builds on the desktop stack merged as #8954. The diff against main is this PR alone: `c391973cf`, plus `d81149783`, `fe2121458`, `378d0e33a`, `160d9d961`, `7bd3a0dbb`, `bfc8dc217`, `fc00f7bc5` and `a2b085712`, which fix the review findings. `c391973cf` is about 1,250 hand-written lines plus 900 of tests and 350 of docs. If it's too big to review, it splits cleanly into three: (1) the zip view with its parity tests, (2) selectors and tolerance, (3) keyed diffs and the draft.

## Summary

Desktop task checks can now verify documents saved as zip archives, such as FreeCAD's `.FCStd` and ODF, OOXML or EPUB files. They can also name XML elements instead of positions, and compare numbers with a tolerance. Until now a zipped document was one opaque `binary` file, so no task about its contents could be checked.

## Problem and expected behavior

A FreeCAD capture showed the gap. Cutting a hole into a plate changes `Document.xml` inside `plate.FCStd`: it gains a `Part::Cylinder` named `Hole` with `Radius` 5, and a `Part::Cut`. REA saw only that the file changed. Reading the XML by hand worked, but pointers by position broke: the radius sits at a different index in FreeCAD 0.21 and 1.0, and the plate's element moves after the edit. Values are strings, so there was no numeric tolerance either.

After this change, the hole task is written once and verified on both versions:

```json
{"name":"cut-hole","prompt":"Cut a 10 mm hole through the middle of the plate and save it.","checks":[
 {"id":"cut","kind":"value_equals","file":"Documents/plate.FCStd",
  "pointer":"/entries/[name=Document.xml]/view/root/children/[name=Objects]/children/[name=Object][@type=Part::Cut]/attributes/type","value":"Part::Cut"},
 {"id":"radius","kind":"value_equals","file":"Documents/plate.FCStd",
  "pointer":"/entries/[name=Document.xml]/view/root/children/[name=ObjectData]/children/[name=Object][@name=Hole]/children/[name=Properties]/children/[name=Property][@name=Radius]/children/[name=Float]/attributes/value","value":5,"tolerance":0.01}]}
```

## Change and scope

- **Zip view.** A file starting with a zip local header gets format `zip` and the view `{entries:[{name,size,sha256,format,view,view_error}], entry_count, truncated}`. Entries keep archive order. Each one is read by the existing readers within their limits.
    - **Limits:** at most 1,000 entries listed, 16 MiB per entry, 100× expansion, and 64 MiB read per archive. Only stored or deflated entries are read, and nothing is extracted to disk.
    - **No nesting:** SQLite, dconf or zip entries inside an archive get a `view_error`.
    - **Shared zip code:** the TypeScript reader uses zip.js on the digest-checked bytes, with `ZipArtifactReader`'s options and name decoding, which are now exported.
    - **Python:** the exported reader uses `zipfile` with the same limits, order and messages.
- **Selectors.** A pointer segment applied to an array may be `[KEY=VALUE]` (a member's string field) or `[@KEY=VALUE]` (one of its attributes). Conditions chain.
    - A selector must match exactly one member. Several matches fail the check with a message naming the selector.
    - Zero matches fail `value_equals`. For `value_absent`, zero matches at the last segment passes, which is how "this element was removed" is written. Zero matches earlier in the pointer still fail.
    - A bracketed segment on an object is still an ordinary key, so existing pointers are unchanged.
- **Tolerance.** `value_equals` takes an optional `tolerance >= 0` with a numeric `value`. It compares numbers and numeral strings, and fails other values as "not a number".
- **Diffs and draft.**
    - **Diffs:** changes inside zip views are listed by selector, using a key unique in both versions. Diffing stays bounded, as in #8875.
    - **Draft:** the task draft suggests whole added or removed elements, then changed values. It never addresses an element by position, and skips namespaced XML.
- **Docs.** The state, tasks and export guides, the specs, a new `document-views` spec folder, and the product skill reference.
- **Review fixes** (`d81149783`, `fe2121458`, `378d0e33a`, `160d9d961`, `7bd3a0dbb`, `bfc8dc217`):
    - **Partial views.** A selector check is undecided while an array it searched may be missing members (a cut listing, or a truncated XML or entry view), in both evaluators.
    - **Pairing.** Diffs pair two versions' members one to one (`pairMembers`), so two new elements can't both match one old element and hide an addition.
    - **Draft.** It descends into JSON values and readable entries added whole, and rejects any positional step that lands on an element, the last step included.
    - **Namespace refusal.** It also checks XML entries inside the value the pointer names, such as the whole listing.
    - **Python reader.** It keeps REA's 500-level JSON depth limit per entry, checked with one iterator per level so it copies no wide list, and calls an entry whose data runs past its declared size damaged.
    - **Type changes and empty values.** An array that becomes an object is compared in place, so values still present no longer look removed. An added empty array or object is checked by equality.
    - **Entries without a view.** A check into an entry's view is decided only when the entry was read in a format that has one. A binary or unread entry fails with the reason in both evaluators, and the draft suggests nothing inside it.
    - **REA's JSON depth check** (from #8875) keeps one iterator per level, like the Python one: 800,000 nulls need 18 MiB instead of more than 64.
    - **Bounded zip reads.** The Python reader inflates an entry at most 64 KiB at a time and stops one byte past its declared size: a 32 KiB archive declaring one byte went from 77.5 MiB to 0.1 MiB.
    - **Metadata checks export.** The namespace refusal applies only to checks that depend on an entry's XML, so checks on an entry's `name`, `size` or `sha256`, or on its absence, export.
    - **Pointer rules in diffs.** Diffs find counterparts by the evaluator's own pointer step, through an index built once per compared array, so a selector across a type change no longer reports a present value removed (20,000 keys against 20,000 members: 31 ms).
    - **Bounded zip directories.** Both readers read the central directory a record at a time and keep the first 1,000 file records, so an archive of 600,000 empty entries peaks at 1.3 MiB in Python (was 293.6 MiB) and needs 24 MiB of heap in REA. The Python zip reader moves to `appExportPythonZip.ts`. Both follow a Zip64 locator just before the end record whether or not the classic record holds sentinels, as zipfile does.
    - **Bounded selector lookups.** A record's selector keys are resolved together, grouped by field set, so retained memory grows with the keys, not members × field sets (76 MB to 4.9 MB on the reported case).
- **Second review fixes** (`fc00f7bc5`, `a2b085712`):
    - **Identity-first pairing.** An element with an identifier (`name`, `id`, `xid`, `*:id`) is keyed only by its tag and identifiers, so an unchanged id still pairs an edited element, and two objects of one type are never paired as a rename. A selector is used only when it matches one sibling, counted over every attribute of every sibling.
    - **Lazy selectors.** Candidates keep the tag apart from each attribute condition and spell only the chosen selector: a 38,588-character tag with 2,000 attributes pairs in 4 ms and 1 MiB instead of 7 s and 148 MiB.
    - **Parsed-view limit first.** Both readers decide JSON with a scanner that builds no value and refuse a view over 4 MiB before building it, in files and entries: a 4.2 MB entry peaks at 8.4 MB in the exported reader instead of 110 MB.
    - **Deep text.** The exported reader confirms the whole text is JSON before reporting a nesting depth error, as REA reads it.

## Contract and boundary impact

- **Semantic owner and earliest changed stage:** `inspect_desktop_application_state` (new `zip` format), then task checks and the export.
- **Contribution scope fit and linked maintainer decision:** same approved desktop-environments work as #8874.
- **CLI and MCP/tool-catalog contract:** unchanged commands; task files accept selectors and `tolerance`.
- **Provider, bridge, target-format, or platform compatibility:** the exported Python reader and `verify.py` gain the same view and checks; parity tests compare them.
- **Evidence, artifact, provenance, or reconstruction contract:** a new `zip` view format; older views are unchanged.
- **Target selection, authority, upstream behavior, and cleanup details:** archives are read from the digest-checked retained bytes, never extracted.
- **Generated metadata:** none.

Expected effects:

- [x] Read existing files or captured data.
- [ ] Launch or attach to a process.
- [ ] Inject instrumentation or run scripts/code.
- [ ] Change process memory, registers, files, or configuration.
- [ ] Contact network services.
- [ ] Recover protected code or work around protections.
- [ ] Documentation or usability only; no target interaction.
- [ ] Not sure yet; investigation or maintainer guidance needed.

## Evidence and regression coverage

All 14 new tests and 2 new test files fail on the parent commit, and all 51 existing tests in those files still pass there. On the parent, `.FCStd` reads as `binary` in both TypeScript and Python.

- **Parity** (`tests/boundary/providers/desktopZipPython.test.ts`):
    - every entry format;
    - each refusal, a damaged archive, the entry limit and the 64 MiB budget;
    - the FreeCAD 0.21 and 1.0 acceptance, where both evaluators fail before and pass after with identical descriptions;
    - an `.odt` case.
- **Real fixtures:** four FreeCAD `Document.xml` files under `tests/fixtures/freecad/`, unchanged from captures, with a README.
- **Shared check cases:** 24 selector and tolerance cases in `appTaskChecks.fixture.ts`, run by both evaluators.
- **Unit and integration tests:** pointer, zip diff, detection and draft tests. `DesktopArchiveTask.test.ts` goes from the state view through the draft to the export.
- **Real captures (built CLI):**
    - `plate.FCStd` reads as `zip` in every version, with name-addressed change listings.
    - The 0.21 capture exports with the hole task, both checks failing on the seed.
    - `describe-desktop-application-task` drafts 10 selector checks, and the export accepts them.

For evidence-bearing changes:

- [ ] Observed, derived, and inferred claims remain distinguishable.
- [ ] Artifact identity, source provenance, and failed attempts remain preserved.
- [ ] Unsupported, incomplete, unavailable, or uncertain outcomes remain visible.

## Validation performed

- These passed with no lint diagnostics in touched files: `npm run typecheck`, `lint`, `lint:typed`, `format:check`, `build:cached` then `knip`, `jscpd`, `docs:check`, `docs:build`, `verify:test-discovery` and `verify:architecture-guards`.
- Desktop tests with the Python boundary tests: 389 passed and 18 skipped with the review fixes, whose new tests all fail on `c391973cf`. The real FreeCAD 0.21 and 1.0 captures still give identical views in both readers, and the hole checks still fail before and pass after. `desktopZipPython`: 7 passed. Desktop CLI boundary tests: 28 passed.
- A FreeCAD environment built from this branch is being booted and solved on an amd64 host; results will follow in a comment.

## Compatibility, safety, and release

- **Breaking changes or migration steps:** none. Existing pointers behave as before, and existing views are unchanged.

**Known follow-ups:**
- **Namespaced XML:** the exported Python reader still spells namespaced names as `{uri}local`, so checks into ODF, OOXML or EPUB content are refused at export. Draft #8994, stacked on this PR, fixes it.

items.title: fix(artifacts): admit ZIP archives after unclaimed leading bytes
items.body:
**What broke:** `inspect-artifact` and `extract-artifact` refused a valid ZIP behind a script or self-extractor stub as "unsupported binary format", although Info-ZIP, bsdtar and Python read it (#5732).
**Fix:** target resolution and root inventory now locate a trailing single-disk ZIP from its end record, central directory and first local header. This applies only when no other format claims the leading bytes; executable-led files keep their executable route.
**Risk:** low to medium. It is additive for previously refused files. Classification stays unchanged for files any existing format recognizes, and Zip64, split and empty archives still fail closed.

## Summary

Fixes #5732. A ZIP preceded by inert leading bytes, such as a `#!/bin/sh` stub or a self-extractor, was refused before inventory or extraction because ZIP recognition only checked the first four bytes. Both prefix styles in common use now inventory and extract with the same verified member bytes as the plain archive:

- member offsets that include the leading bytes (`zip -A`, or Python's `zipfile` appending to the stub);
- raw concatenation, where offsets were written before the stub was prepended.

## Problem and expected behavior

Trigger: a 17-byte shell stub followed by a ZIP. Before this change, on main `d672cc239` (macOS arm64), `inspect-artifact` returned `target_unavailable` / "Cannot open artifact: unsupported binary format." for both prefix styles, while the plain ZIP passed.

Expected: a file whose leading bytes are claimed by no other format, and which ends in a structurally consistent ZIP, is a ZIP archive. A file whose leading bytes begin an executable header keeps the executable classification. For example, `/bin/ls` with an appended ZIP stays `mach-o-universal`.

## Change and scope

- `src/domain/zipPackageFormat.ts` now owns ZIP recognition at both ends of a file: `hasZipSignature` for the start and the new `locateTrailingZipArchive` for a trailing archive. The locator takes an injected positional read and is bounded to the last 22 + 65,535 bytes, one 46-byte central-directory header and one 4-byte local-header signature. It requires:
  - an end record whose comment ends exactly at end of file;
  - a single disk with at least one entry and no Zip64 markers;
  - a central-directory header at the derived position;
  - a local header at the first entry's offset, using an offset shift that resolves both prefix styles.
- `src/domain/binaryTarget.ts` adds `claimsExecutableHeader`, which recognizes the ELF, MZ, Mach-O and FAT families that `parseExecutableHeader` interprets, whether or not the header is valid. Both callers use it, so they make the same decision.
- `BinaryTargetResolver` consults the locator only after native header detection fails and only when no executable family claims the leading bytes. Root inventory classification (`classify.ts`) consults it only when the bytes classify as `file` or `unknown` and no executable family claims them.
- `ZIP_NON_ENTRY_LIMITATION` now names leading bytes before the first entry, such as a self-extractor stub, as non-entry bytes that are not occurrences.
- Not included:
  - Zip64, split, and empty trailing archives, which stay refused;
  - trailing data after the end record;
  - nested members, whose classification still uses their own leading bytes;
  - executable-led archives such as PE or ELF self-extractors, which keep their executable route.

  Admitting any of these would need a separate decision.
- Scope decision: not applicable. This is format recognition within the existing ZIP reader boundary. The reader (`@zip.js/zip.js` 2.15.0) already reads both prefix styles, as verified below.

## Contract and boundary impact

- Semantic owner and earliest changed stage: ZIP recognition in `src/domain/zipPackageFormat.ts`, consumed by target resolution and root inventory classification.
- Contribution scope fit and linked maintainer decision: not applicable (ordinary fix).
- CLI and MCP/tool-catalog contract: no schema change. Previously refused files with unclaimed leading bytes and a trailing ZIP now return `zip` artifact inventories and extractions.
- Provider, bridge, target-format, or platform compatibility: classification is unchanged for every file another format recognizes. Executable-led files with appended archives keep their executable route.
- Evidence, artifact, provenance, or reconstruction contract: root identity and digest cover the whole file, leading bytes included. Members keep their content identities. The ZIP limitation now names leading bytes as non-entry bytes.
- Target selection, authority, upstream behavior, and cleanup details: no new process, write or network behavior. Extraction still uses the hardened ZIP reader and output tree.
- Generated metadata, package, or installation impact: none.

  - `tests/acceptance/artifactZipLeadingBytes.test.ts`: the public CLI `inspect-artifact` and `extract-artifact` on a script-stubbed ZIP. It checks `zip` root format, verified members, the non-entry limitation, and the extracted bytes. This fails on the base revision with `target_unavailable`.

items.title: fix(artifacts): report ZIP bytes the central directory does not account for
items.body:
## Summary

The ZIP reader builds its listing only from the central directory (zip.js `getEntriesGenerator`). When a local file entry has no record in that directory, its bytes were silently skipped and the traversal still reported `complete`. This PR declares ZIP coverage `complete` only when the central directory's records account for every byte before the directory. When they do not, coverage is `unknown`, with a limitation that gives the unaccounted byte count, the number of ranges and the first offset.

Builds on #10572 (merged), which makes readers declare coverage; this branch is rebased onto `main` and carries only its own commits. Refs structural audit plan 1.6 (ZIP remainder) and report 12 row 9b.

## Problem and expected behavior

Fixture runs on `main`, with stored members built by hand. Every shape listed only the central-directory members and reported no coverage gap:

| Shape | Listed | Coverage before | Coverage now |
|---|---|---|---|
| hidden local entry between two listed members | `a.txt,b.txt` | complete (silent) | unknown, 56 bytes at offset 46 |
| hidden local entry before the first member | `a.txt` | complete | unknown, offset 0 |
| hidden local entry after the last member | `a.txt` | complete | unknown |
| record beyond the EOCD's declared count | `a.txt` | complete | unknown |
| shell stub prepended before the first member | all | complete | unknown, stub bytes at offset 0 |

**Real-world case (observed).** `jadx-headless-mcp-0.7.1-all.jar` is a shaded fat jar with 23,368 members. It holds five local entries that its central directory does not list: `META-INF/LICENSE.txt`, `LICENSE` (×3) and `META-INF/LICENSE`. These are duplicates the shading tool dropped from the directory but left in the file. This PR reports them as `unknown`, 20,104 bytes in 5 ranges.

## Change and scope

Two approaches were possible:
- (a) Account for byte ranges and report `unknown` when bytes are unaccounted.
- (b) Keep `complete` and add a limitation saying the listing is relative to the central directory.

I chose (a). (b) would keep `complete` on archives that demonstrably hold unlisted entries, as the jar above shows, and would add a sentence to every ZIP inventory. (a) costs about 120 lines in one module.

- `src/artifacts/ZipMemberRegion.ts` (new) owns the accounting. `accountZipMemberRegion` sorts the directory's records by local-header offset and reads each 30-byte local header to get the exact name and extra-field lengths. It then checks that the records tile `[0, directoryOffset)`:
  - Bytes that hold a data descriptor (12, 16, 20 or 24) after a record whose descriptor flag is set are accounted for.
  - A well-formed APK Signature Scheme v2+ block ending at the directory is accounted for: `APK Sig Block 42` magic, and leading and trailing sizes that agree.
  - Overlapping records are left to zip.js's existing overlap refusal when the data is read.
  - A record whose local header is missing is counted and reported separately.
  - Header reads share 64 KiB windows, so adjacent small members need one read.

items.title: fix(desktop): preserve ZIP member identity across bounded readers
items.body:
Fixes #10172.

A ZIP member can carry two CRC-matching Unicode Path fields, first `hidden/`, then `settings.json`. The complete ZIP decoder sees a regular file, but desktop preflight selected the first field and reported an empty, untruncated view. With an ordinary seed and this affected end archive, the compiled export CLI accepted a false task asserting that `settings.json` had been removed.

The root cause is conflicting interpretation at the bounded directory boundary: zip.js selects the final extra field by ID, whereas both preflights returned the first one. Python's library additionally interprets each occurrence and can retain an earlier valid name or reject superseded UTF-8.

- Select the final Unicode Path claim before validating version, CRC and UTF-8, preserving the UTF-8 flag's precedence and stored-name fallback.
- In the generated directory owner, use one exact decoded name for classification and the retained view. Other fields, comments, local-header checks and original artifact bytes remain intact.

## Summary

Fixes #5489

Adds a dry-run planning mode (`dry_run: true` / `--dry-run`) to `extract_artifact` so agents and operators can inspect what an extraction will materialize, verify destination admission and path-collision rules, and review labeled byte estimates before touching disk.

## Problem and expected behavior

- **Smallest trigger:** Call `extract_artifact` (or CLI `rea extract-artifact`) when evaluating an archive or application package before deciding whether to materialize files on disk.
- **Violated invariant:** Previously, `extract_artifact` always staged and moved extracted entries into `output_root`, providing no dry-run mode to validate destination path safety (Windows/POSIX reserved characters, NFC collisions, prefix collisions) and inspect planned vs. unsupported/unresolved entries without writing to disk.
- **Expected behavior:** When `dry_run: true` (or `--dry-run`) is passed, `extract_artifact` validates `output_root` admission via `SafeOutputTree.checkDestination(input.outputRoot)`, traverses selected entries using the same `normalizeDestinationPath` and `ArtifactPathRegistry` rules as real extraction, creates zero destination directories/files or sidecar manifests, and returns a structured `plan` alongside `dry_run: true`.

items.body:
> **Independent of #3586** (JVM debug metadata). This branch is cut from `main` and carries only the DEX tool, so either PR can merge first. The few helpers both readers need are shared modules introduced here: the modified-UTF8 decoder, archive-member selection and reading, and the magic peek. Whichever PR merges second will merge `main` and adopt them in place of its own copies. Both PRs also carry the same shared ZIP-reader changes: `storedPath` is the raw central-directory name, a member is a directory only when its stored name ends in `/`, and the abort reason is kept as the cancellation cause. In `ZipArtifactReader.ts` they differ by one line, `normalizeArchiveMemberPath` here against the equivalent `./` strip in #3586; the second to merge keeps `normalizeArchiveMemberPath`.

## Summary

Closes #4538.

Adds `inspect_dex_debug_metadata` (CLI `rea inspect-dex-debug-metadata`), the Android DEX sibling of `inspect_jvm_debug_metadata` (#3586). It statically reports the compiler-emitted debug metadata in a selected local `.dex`, or the `classes*.dex` members of an APK/ZIP. That lets an analyst judge **debugging readiness before attaching a debugger or reading a decompilation**: do source files, line positions, parameter names and local-variable names, types and scopes survive, or were they stripped by R8/ProGuard?

## Problem and expected behavior

When triaging an APK, the first practical question is whether there is debug metadata to work with: a debug build, a release build with line numbers kept, or a fully stripped R8 release. Today that takes `dexdump` from the Android SDK and manual counting, and an agent can't get it as Evidence.

## Change and scope

The tool works at two granularities. A DEX holds thousands of classes, so neither alone is enough.

- **Summary (default):** one entry per DEX member. For an APK, these are the members ART's multidex loader loads: `classes.dex`, `classes2.dex`, … while each is present under its exact stored central-directory name. The raw name is used, never an Info-ZIP Unicode Path name. At most 64 members are read; past that, REA refuses and asks for `entry`. It gives method tallies, line positions, local declarations (with `explicit_local_declarations` separating locals the stream declares from the implicit `this`/parameter locals), distinct source-file names, and a derived `readiness` of `present`, `partial`, `stripped` or `unknown`. `unknown` means unreadable sections with no present evidence; it is never reported as absent.
- **Per-class detail (`class_descriptor` = `Lpkg/Name;`):** each method's `name` and JVM-form `descriptor`, plus its `locals` (name, type, signature, register, scope, `out_of_range`). Locals include the implicit `this` and the parameters with their parameter names, resolved exactly as `dexdump` resolves them.

How the code is laid out:

- **Domain** (`src/domain/dex/`, dependency-free, `Result` plus tagged errors): DEX framing, the `debug_info_item` state machine, a string/type resolver, and summary/detail assembly.
- **Shared helpers:** `src/domain/modifiedUtf8.ts` (MUTF-8, used by DEX `string_data_item` and JVM class files alike), `src/artifacts/archiveMember.ts` and `peekArtifactMagic`. Each has one owner, ready for the JVM reader to adopt.

**Bounds** (each limit and its reason is in `src/dex/DexFileRelease.ts`):

- One call-wide decode budget of 64 Mi debug opcodes covers every method and member. Identical debug streams are decoded once.
- The summary only counts, with no per-position or per-local allocation.
- The class detail projects its serialized size from memoised per-string bounds while it decodes, and refuses before building past the 8 MiB output budget. The exact check is kept as a backstop.
- Members are read, analysed and released one at a time.
- Class-data parsing is charged to that budget too. Memo maps and the distinct-source count have fixed ceilings, and a local's register must lie inside the method's frame. Decoding is cooperative. It yields in bounded slices, including during class_data validation, so cancellation lands within one slice: the worst crafted member stalls the event loop for about 47 ms, and cancellation settles in under 1 ms. A class_data entry's cumulative index must stay inside its id table, which is ART's `CheckIndex`.
- Every text path is byte-bounded:
  - named members and spellings: at most 128 names or 4 KiB, with the rest counted;
  - display names over 160 UTF-16 units: shortened by start and end with a marker (reported `entry` values are never shortened);
  - archive-reader notes: at most 1,024 characters each and 8 KiB in total;
  - `class_descriptor` echoes: shortened the same way.

  The 8 MiB output bound counts the result and its repeated `limitations`.

**Member selection with `entry`:**
- `entry` matches the stored name, with a leading `./` optional. The exactly-stored spelling wins; otherwise ambiguity is refused and the stored spellings are listed.
- Members REA cannot read are refused as `unsupported_target` "unavailable, not absent": ZIP directories, encrypted members, and members stored with a symbolic-link mode, which ART loads but REA does not read.
- Skipped-member notes mark names that `entry` would refuse, and advise `entry` only while a selectable member remains.
- Reader notes, such as a Unicode Path name differing from the stored name, or directory attributes, are carried into the result.

**Not included:** `odex`/`vdex`/`oat`/`cdex` (refused), nested non-root DEX auto-selection (pass `entry`), `mapping.txt` deobfuscation, and runtime/JDWP debugging.

## Contract and boundary impact

- **Semantic owner and earliest changed stage:** new `src/domain/dex/` modules, plus the shared helpers above (one owner each).
- **Contribution scope fit:** static, read-only inspection of a caller-selected local file. No Android code executes, no device or `adb` is involved, nothing is mutated, so no scope decision is required. This draft invites one anyway.
- **CLI and MCP/tool-catalog contract:** adds one tool and command with Evidence parity, which the real lane asserts. The catalog is regenerated.
- **Evidence contract:** confidence is `observed`, the subject is path, format and SHA-256, and the service re-validates identity. Archive Evidence names the selected member.
- **Generated metadata:** produced by the normal scripts; skill sources are edited under `.agents/skills/`.

Expected effects:

- [x] Read existing files or captured data.
- [ ] Launch or attach to a process.
- [ ] Inject instrumentation or run scripts/code.
- [ ] Change process memory, registers, files, or configuration.
- [ ] Contact network services.
- [ ] Recover protected code or work around protections.
- [ ] Documentation or usability only; no target interaction.
- [ ] Not sure yet; investigation or maintainer guidance needed.

## Evidence and regression coverage

**Real toolchain lane** (`npm run verify:dex`): passes 14 cases. Using the Android SDK's `d8` and `dexdump` plus a JDK, it:

- compiles an owned fixture with `-g` and `-g:none` and dexes each
- cross-checks the decoded facts against `dexdump`, including the `this` and parameter local tuples
- covers APK summarize-all and entry selection
- runs CLI and stdio MCP in Evidence parity, with the advertised schema validated

**Independent review:** it caught a blocking correctness bug. Implicit parameter locals weren't seeded, which dropped every parameter and `this` from debug builds. After the fix, a real debug APK's locals went from 57,505 to 155,804, and its line positions from 198,768 to **204,456, exactly `dexdump`'s count**.

**Adversarial audits:** independent passes ran after every fix round, and every finding is fixed in this PR. Later rounds fixed:
- un-paced class_data validation;
- an over-cap refusal blamed on Android;
- member selection by Unicode Path name instead of the stored name (ART uses the raw name);
- dropped reader notes;
- a count bound that refused ART-valid class_data;
- a public CLI/MCP regression when selecting a `./`-stored member;
- symlink-mode members silently dropped;
- unbounded text (a 7.7 MB refusal, now 4.2 KB);
- dead-end `entry` advice;
- a short non-DEX file (a 111-byte text decoy in a blind-triage exercise) refused as a "truncated DEX": the magic is now identified on whatever bytes exist before any length check, compact dex is named only from the full 4-byte `cdex`, and the truncation message states the bytes needed and present.

The final audit at head `0f6c7194f` passed 1,758 public CLI + stdio MCP cases with no adapter failure, schema violation or CLI/MCP divergence, and no wrong-member answer: every reported entry's SHA-256 equals the raw member bytes. The checks compare REA with an ART-style selection model; its 32 non-agreements are all expected. 24 are documented refusals of symlink-mode members. 8 are an APK with an invalid UTF-8 flagged name, which ART also refuses and the model doesn't handle. The numbers below are measured on each auditor's own inputs, under a 256 MB heap where noted.

| Attack | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Class detail, 76 KB (2,000 locals sharing a 64 KiB name) | 1,249 MB peak; fatal OOM under a 256 MB heap | refused in 9 ms at 66 MB, including under 256 MB |
| 1,000 locals × 256 KiB name (quadratic resolver) | 18.6 s | 9 ms |
| Summary of a 2 MB file (2 billion positions via shared streams) | 55 s, 878 MB | 27 ms, 70 MB, with identical counts |
| 16 MB DEX declaring 8M proto parameters | 1.8 GB (2.35 GB in detail mode); fatal OOM under 256 MB | 36 ms at 97 MB under 256 MB (proto refused as malformed, over Dalvik's 255 argument registers) |
| 40 MB DEX with `parameters_size` = 40M | 1.2 GB; fatal OOM under 256 MB | 62 ms at 143 MB |
| 500 classes sharing an inflated class_data (field count over filler) | 85 s, un-cancellable | 3 ms (impossible count refused up front; parsing charged) |
| 1.5M methods with distinct debug streams (49.5 MB) | fatal OOM under 256 MB (memo `Map`) | completes in 1.5 s; memo capped |
| 2M locals in distinct registers (11 MB) | 332 MB | 81 MB (registers bounded by `registers_size`) |
| 4M methods in one class (15 MiB) | fatal OOM under 256 MB | 1.25 s at 72 MB (classes and methods are streamed, never materialised) |
| 2M methods sharing a 255-parameter proto | 13.9 s | 0.64 s (O(1) memo key) |
| 2.09M class_defs (64 MiB) | 353 MB | 115 MB |

**Checked against `dexdump` on a real R8 release APK.** This surfaced two semantic bugs, both fixed here:

- Positions past a method's code were counted. R8 shares debug streams across methods, which inflated line positions about 3×: 4,497,768 against `dexdump`'s 1,468,433. Only positions with `address < insns_size` are counted now, giving 1,473,289. The remaining 0.2–0.7% on R8 members is `dexdump` stopping at the start of a method's last instruction; this is documented. Debug builds match exactly.
- Zero-length scopes, which kotlinc leaves when it re-declares a generic parameter at address 0, were counted as locals. That put `local_declarations` 12% above `dexdump` on a real Kotlin debug APK. They're skipped now, and locals match `dexdump` **exactly on all 15 real DEX members** checked.
- A single work budget shared across members falsely refused a legitimate 16 × 10 MB multidex app. Each member now gets a budget proportional to its own bytes; real members use at most 22% of it.
- `readiness` counted the implicit `this` and parameter locals, so that release APK read as `present`. It now reads `stripped`. `local_declarations` keeps exact `dexdump` parity (115,191 = 115,191), and the new `explicit_local_declarations` drives readiness.

The real lane now includes a `d8 --release` build and asserts **exact** equality with `dexdump` on line positions and locals for both debug and release builds.

**Review round (head `15e098095`):** all 7 automated review findings were fixed, each with a test that fails on `c936fdca5`, followed by two independent audit rounds:

- an unreadable proto parameter list makes the method `malformed` (readiness `unknown`), never `present`;
- every string reference in a debug stream (parameter names, local name/type/signature, `DBG_SET_FILE`) must name a readable string, as ART's verifier requires; validity is memoised per `string_data` offset;
- the fixed 2,000,000-opcode guard is gone; each opcode is charged to the work budget, and the walk is resumable, pausing mid-stream when the pacer's slice is due (a 30M-opcode stream's longest stall fell from about 0.35 s to 26 ms; an abort at 100 ms lands within 1 ms);
- every class_def visit costs a work unit, so a long table of empty classes yields;
- a later member's refusal, cancellation or failed read keeps the completed members' summaries as a `dex-debug-metadata-members` partial observation, retained on the primary failure so a confirmed cleanup keeps it;
- `entry` advice counts only selectable members;
- acceptance tests assert facts and owning formatters instead of whole sentences.

The audits also aligned `DBG_END_LOCAL`/`DBG_RESTART_LOCAL` with ART's `DecodeDebugLocalInfo` and drop locals still live when a stream breaks partway, as `dexdump` does. 880 methods from 14 compiler-built DEX files match `dexdump` with 0 malformed; pausing and one uninterrupted run agree on all 218,074 methods checked.

**Second review round (head `a51111649`):** 2 more automated findings were fixed. The first, a pacing change, has a test that fails on `15e098095`. Three independent audit rounds followed; the last was clean.

- **Pause on work done, not on an opcode count:** long string checks now pause. The string resolver scans and validates modified UTF-8 in 16 KiB steps and asks the pacer after each step. Paused scans continue on the next call.
- **Each string is scanned once:** validity and the JSON bound come from one memoised scan, charged once. An invalid string is never decoded.
- **Method names and descriptors in class detail** are paced the same way.
- **No decode past the budget:** a decode the budget cannot cover is refused before it runs. The detail re-checks the budget and cancellation after its last decodes.
- **Measured:**
  - Greptile's probe (256 `DBG_SET_FILE` names of 64 KiB) went from 33.5M units before the first yield, against a 262,144-unit slice, to a longest stall of about 1 ms.
  - Detail stalls on 60 MB crafted members fell from about 238 ms to 3 ms, and an abort lands within 1 ms.
  - Pausing changes neither results nor charge: 0 mismatches over 48,790 equivalence runs, 273,565 walked methods and 1,200 mutants.
  - Against `15e098095`, provider output is identical on 43,116 summary and class-detail results.
  - Work charged is equal to or lower than `15e098095` everywhere.
- **Remaining:** a valid string that the budget covers is still decoded unpaced when it goes into a class-detail report. The 8 MiB output limit bounds this to about 350 ms; an abort during it is observed when the decode finishes.
- **Test change:** the CLI acceptance test now imports `INSPECT_DEX_DEBUG_METADATA_CONTRACT` instead of the full catalog.

**Shared ZIP reader change:** a CI fix in this round makes `ZipArtifactReader` add a limitation note to every member whose valid Info-ZIP Unicode Path name differs from its stored name. Every `inventoryArtifact` consumer sees this note; member selection still uses the stored name.

**Remaining proof gaps:**
- In CI without the Android SDK the real lane prints `skipped`.
- Line positions under R8 may be renumbered synthetic lines that need a `mapping.txt`; that is reported, not asserted.

For evidence-bearing changes:

- [x] Observed, derived, and inferred claims remain distinguishable.
- [x] Artifact identity, source provenance, and failed attempts remain preserved.
- [x] Unsupported, incomplete, unavailable, or uncertain outcomes remain visible.

## Validation performed

At head `a51111649` (the second review round; every gate run fresh with `TURBO_FORCE=true`):

- `npm run verify:dex -- --require-tools` (build-tools 36.1, JDK 25): passed, 14 cases against `dexdump`.
- `npm run test:local` on the DEX tests plus `modifiedUtf8`: 152 passed in 11 files.
- `npm run test:focused` on the DEX acceptance and lifecycle tests: 27 passed.
- `npm run check:fast`, `docs:check`, `format:check`, `mcp-catalog:check`, `verify:module-boundaries`: passed.

At head `15e098095` (the review round and two audit rounds on top of `c936fdca5`):

- `npm run verify:dex -- --require-tools` (build-tools 36.1, JDK 25): passed, 14 cases against `dexdump`.
- `npm run test:local` on `src/dex`, `src/domain/dex` and `src/application/dex`: 123 passed.
- `npm run test:focused` on the DEX acceptance and lifecycle tests: 27 passed.
- `npm run check:fast` and `docs:check`: passed.

At head `c936fdca5` (merge of `main` at `bc143125e`):

- Unit tests: DEX and shared 113, artifacts 219, all passed.
- `npm run test:focused`: 249 tests passed across 10 files (DEX acceptance and lifecycle, ZIP acceptance, read-failure precedence, stable-artifact consumers).
- `npm run check:fast`, `docs:check`, `format:check`, `mcp-catalog:check`, `verify:module-boundaries`: passed.
- `DexFileProvider` now reads through `main`'s admitted `StableRegularFileDescriptor`.
- **Merge note:** in the merge commit, the repository's pre-commit hook (`oxlint --fix`) merged duplicate imports in 14 upstream files this PR does not otherwise touch (+38/−32). Behaviour is unchanged.

Earlier heads:

- `npm run check:fast`: passed.
- `npm run test:local` with src/dex, src/domain/dex, src/application/dex and src/artifacts tests: 168 passed at `94b9c6447`. Head `149f342ad` only adds a regression test pinning class_data at end of file as unreadable (`dexDebugMetadata.test.ts`: 27 passed).
- `npm run test:focused -- tests/acceptance/dexDebugMetadataCli.test.ts tests/process-global/dexProviderLifecycle.test.ts`: 26 passed. The magic-order audit drove 384 malformed-input cases through both the CLI and stdio MCP with 0 mismatches. The acceptance tests drive the public CLI and stdio MCP.
- 30 ZIP-consumer test files (inventory, extraction, Flutter, jadx, SAZ, ASAR, Harmony and others): 251 passed at the previous head, after the shared-reader changes.
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run verify:module-boundaries`, `npx knip`: passed.
- `git merge-tree` against current `main`: merges cleanly.
- `npm run verify:dex` at head `94b9c6447`: passed, 14 cases against `dexdump`, including exact equality for debug and `d8 --release` builds.
- `npm run docs:check` and `npm run mcp-catalog:check`: passed.
- Real APKs through the CLI: a debug build reports `present`; a 40 MB, 4-member R8 release reports `stripped` with lines kept, in 1.5 s at 430 MB peak.

**Representative output** (that R8 release APK; first member, sample trimmed):

```json
{
  "container": "apk",
  "members": 4,
  "members[0]": {
    "entry": "classes.dex",
    "bytes": 9983472,
    "summary": {
      "dex_version": "039",
      "class_count": 10255,
      "methods_with_code": 56414,
      "methods_with_debug_info": 55172,
      "methods_with_parameter_names": 0,
```

Updates `@zip.js/zip.js` from 2.15.0 to 2.24.0
Release notes

Sourced from @​zip.js/zip.js's releases.

v2.24.0

What's Changed in v2.24.0

New features

  • The uncompressedSize option of ZipWriter#add() is now read for a ReadableStream or any reader without a size, as the size the stream is expected to have: the entry is then laid out like one read from a reader of that size, i.e. without Zip64 structures below 4 GB and, with bufferedWrite, without a data descriptor. The sizes written remain the measured ones. The option is validated on every path and throws the new ERR_INVALID_UNCOMPRESSED_SIZE_OPTION error when it is not a non-negative integer

Improvements

  • Skip the data descriptor by default when the local header can carry the CRC-32 and the sizes: a passThrough entry read from a reader of known size with crc32 provided (or AES-encrypted, which stores no CRC-32), which also keeps the direct write path instead of a temporary stream, and a reader of unknown size written with bufferedWrite or dataDescriptor: false. ZipCrypto entries, entries copied with the entry option and explicit dataDescriptor: true keep their descriptor
  • Split the Node.js and Deno CI job into three lanes

Documentation

  • State that the duplicates policy of the filesystem imports applies to the entries kept by the filter option only

Full Changelog: https://github.com/gildas-lormeau/zip.js/compare/v2.23.0...v2.24.0

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 noreply@anthropic.com

v2.23.0

What's Changed in v2.23.0

New features

  • Add the filter option to the import*() methods of ZipFS and ZipDirectoryEntry: the function receives each entry read from the zip file and returns true (or a promise resolving to true) to import it. It can read the data of the entry to decide, and the entries left out never reach the duplicates policy
  • Add the filter option to the export*() methods and to getExportedSize(): the function receives each ZipEntry of the tree and returns true to export it. Leaving out a directory leaves out its subtree, the entries left out are not read and are not counted by onprogress and onentryprogress
  • Add the filter option to exportFileSystemHandle(), with the same semantics as the zip exports
  • Add the filter option to addFileSystemHandle() and addFileSystemEntry(): the function receives each handle found and its path, so a directory like node_modules or hidden files can be left out without walking them

Full Changelog: https://github.com/gildas-lormeau/zip.js/compare/v2.22.1...v2.23.0

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 noreply@anthropic.com

v2.22.1

What's Changed in v2.22.1

Bug fixes

  • A zip file written behind a prefix which was removed together with its whole first entry, like a self-extracting page whose first entry is the face shown by the host, is read again: the entries are shifted to their real positions and their data can be read. Since v2.21.0, the shift was decided on the first central directory record only, and a first record whose local file header lies in the removed bytes proves nothing, so the entries kept their stored offsets and getData() failed with ERR_LOCAL_FILE_HEADER_NOT_FOUND, whatever the strictness option. The reader now checks the following records until one settles the question, and keeps the protection against a damaged end of central directory record whose local file headers are right
  • An entry which lies before the start of the zip file after such a shift is no longer reported as WARNING_UNSORTED_CENTRAL_DIRECTORY

items.body:
# feat(flutter): identify Dart snapshot builds and inspect AOT payloads by pure APK parsing

Opens the untouched Flutter lane — no PR, issue, or roadmap entry had covered Dart/Flutter analysis before. Four commits: two features, one ownership hardening matching the bar applied across the merged JEB/ADB/Apktool PRs, and one inherited-main fix.

## `identify_flutter_build` — build identification

Reads an APK's `lib/<abi>/libapp.so` and `libflutter.so` through the hardened ZIP reader and reports:

- **The Dart VM snapshot hash** — read 20 bytes after every Dart snapshot magic (`f5 f5 dc dc`). The vm and isolate sections are both found and **cross-checked**: agreeing sections collapse to one `snapshot_hash`; disagreeing sections keep every value in `snapshot_hash_candidates` with `snapshot_hash: null` and partial coverage rather than silently picking one.
- **Per-ABI library digests and sizes**, the engine's **GNU build-id**, and any *labeled* strings (`Dart VM version: …`, Android clang/LLVM toolchain lines) — verbatim; release builds strip the Dart string and absence is reported as `null`, not guessed.
- A target with no `libapp.so` reports `flutter_detected: false` with **complete** coverage — absence is an answer.

## `inspect_dart_aot` — AOT payload inspection

For one ABI's `libapp.so` (caller-selected; default arm64-v8a → x86_64 → first available):

- **Snapshot sections** — the four `_kDart*Snapshot*` symbols located through the **ELF dynamic symbol table** (ELF32 *and* ELF64 little-endian, bounds-checked; payloads without exported symbols are refused), each with file offset and size.
- **Data-section headers** validated (magic, kind, length); instructions sections carry a different layout and report `null` for those fields — honestly.
- **A bounded string-pool projection from the isolate data section**: distinct `package:` source URIs (the app's dependency inventory), `dart:` SDK URIs, and identifier-shaped tokens — labeled a **byte-pattern projection, not deserialized cluster semantics**; typed recovery needs an SDK-specific parser, which the snapshot hash unlocks.

## Ownership hardening (mirrors the merged PRs' bar)

- **Owned read-only snapshots**: the admitted APK is copied (EXCL, `chmod 0400`) before digesting and parsing; every read uses the snapshot, so concurrent modification cannot mix into one observation. Failed snapshot cleanup is **retained and retried on `close()`** (aggregate error when still owned); root removal is injectable for tests.
- **Bounded-before-allocation**: the AOT image buffer is allocated at exactly the declared size before reading (256 MiB ceiling), and cancellation is checked between digest and stream chunks through a captured abort reason.
- Tests cover paths containing spaces, cleanup retention with close retry, and cancellation before any root is created.

## Inherited-main fix (first commit, independently cherry-pickable)

The merged ADB family advertises five patterns with unescaped dashes in character classes (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]`), which unicodeSets-mode clients reject — the advertised-patterns boundary test is red on current `main` for `read_adb_setting` and `start_adb_activity`. Escaped the same way the JEB fix did, and restored the Italian README's analysis-table rows (JEB/ADB/Apkktool/Flutter) that the recent merges added everywhere else, keeping its link set identical to `README.md`.

## Verification

- **Real target**: Flutter Gallery 2.9.2 (112 MB, three ABIs) via `npm run verify:flutter` — agreeing hash `65817c30a78bb44c3dc3771876b6010a` on every ABI, per-ABI build-ids, all four snapshot symbols on **both ELF64 and ELF32** images, header validation, hash agreement between both tools, and the 756/201 URI string pool; a plain aapt2-built APK reports not-detected with complete coverage.
- **30 provider/scanner/ELF/service tests** (goldens from the real libraries, real zips built in-test, chunk-boundary double-count coverage) plus CLI/MCP boundary schemas (Ajv-validated examples, unknown input rejected, v-mode portability).
- `check:fast`, `docs:generate`, `docs:check`, 3,632 tests across domain/services/adapters/composition, and the product catalog all pass on this branch.

Towards the Flutter gap in the #717 Android roadmap discussion. No engine, SDK, or tool installation; no new runtime dependencies; pure parsing only.
